newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds follow markets higher on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds follow markets higher on U.S. data.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed on Wednesday amid good demand, rising along with other bond markets as a sharp drop in U.S. factory gate prices eased concerns about rising U.S interest rates, dealers said.
Gilts also shot higher after U.S. producer prices fell 0.6 pct, the biggest drop since August 1993. Treasuries led the UK market back into positive ground.

"The Irish market is very spread-driven today in relation to the markets around us," a dealer said "We've seen strong buying against Spain on the back of a very good Spanish inflation figure, and also against Denmark."
There was also increasingly strong demand for longer-end bonds, the dealer said.
"I think people are realising that time is marching on and they want to get into longer yields over the 18 months to EMU."

By 1500 GMT, the Irish 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 13 pence from Tuesday's close at 102.48 to yield 5.84 percent, while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 30 pence from the close at 110.00 to yield 6.53 percent.

With the Irish pound higher against the Deutschemark on Thursday -- which weakened on doubts over Germany meeting EMU criteria on time -- the short end of the Irish bond market had stabilised, dealers said.
Looking ahead, dealers said, the market would continue to focus on inflation-indicative data, including U.S. jobless figures, and the Philadelphia Fed Survey later in the week.
Also, on Thursday the National Treasury Management Agency is due to announce the amount and maturity date of stock to be auctioned on May 20.
Dealers said they expected the stock to be short-end, most likely five-year bonds.
